history.value: What a net can see is the vocabulary saved with it. The product net (10-29) reads 27 effect scalars and 8 triggers of today's 48 and 19: content using a newer atom loses that effect scalar (dropped) or lands in the one unknown slot (triggers, conditions, cards, powers); Burn's cost for being held at turn end (damage_plain_self) is among the dropped, so to the product net a Burn is an unplayable card with no effect. A monster's inputs are its HP, block, powers and the intent on show (Hexaghost's Divider damage included); the moves after the shown intent are opt-in: pattern rows ("row_kinds": ["pattern"] or "extra_rows": true in a finetune config; one row per possible next move with its probability and effects) and the lookahead columns, both off in every net read up to 2026-11-06, so the place in a move cycle is visible only through the combat turn count. finetune.py widens the parent to today's vocabulary for source configs and Silent content (vocab_for; the boss bursts ubb-* have all 48 scalars) and keeps the parent's vocabulary for mutated monsters and generated packs (kept_vocab): a burst on a pack mechanic built from newer atoms (static, countdown, replacement and pattern rows, picks, expression amounts, the triggers RoundEnd, OwnerAttacked, OwnerPlaysCard, OwnerAttackHit) cannot see it until that path widens too, and a bench on such content would measure blindness, not adaptation. On the monsters rung SharpHide and Ritual are fully visible to the product net; Thorns and WeakOnHit share the unknown trigger slot with known effects.
